newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico to boost natgas exports 100-150 mln cfd.
newsitem.headline: Mexico to boost natgas exports 100-150 mln cfd.

text.p: Increased natural gas processing capacity should soon allow Mexico to boost exports of the fuel by 100 to 150 million cubic feet per day (cfd), the director general of state-owned oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) said on Thursday.
"In the coming months we will be able to increase the volume of exports," Director General Adrian Lajous told a news conference. He later added the estimate of an additional 100 to 150 million cfd.

Mexico has traditionally imported more natural gas than it exports, although the gap has narrowed in recent months. In April, Mexico imported an average 98.9 million cfd, compared to exports of five million cfd.

Lajous spoke in this southeastern city at the inauguration of a renovated natural gas procesing plant in the Cactus complex, which processes about one-third of the nation's natural gas. Expansion should add 1.2 billion cfd capacity in the region in the next three months, he said.
But most of the added capacity will be used to produce natural gas for the domestic market, Lajous said.
"The basic objective is for domestic use," he said. "We foresee a substantial increase in Mexico's natural gas consumption."
Mexico is promoting the fuel as a cleaner alternative to fuel oil and liquified petroleum gas (LPG). Environmental norms set to take effect in 1998 are fueling the substitution efforts.
